Strait of Hormuz Status: September 30, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  213 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
30 September 2026 .
Brent $ 102.90 -2.26 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 UA.NEWS reports an Indian seafarer was killed in the Strait of Hormuz in the September 23 strike on the bulk carrier Cape Dao; MEA says 163 Indian seafarers remain aboard 12 vessels in the Persian Gulf, per morungexpress.com.

02 Brent stood at $102.90, down 2.26%, as of 02:57 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

03 Iraq is importing petrol via Syria's Baniyas port as a bypass route, per India Today; ABC10 reports U.S.-Iran talks continue after President Trump rejected Iran's strait-reopening proposal.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic, with IMF PortWatch recording 1 transit on 2026-09-27 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $102.90, a move of -2.26%, as of 02:57 UTC. The September 23 strike on the bulk carrier Cape Dao continues to draw coverage: UA.NEWS reports an Indian seafarer was killed in that attack, and morungexpress.com reports MEA says 163 Indian seafarers are currently aboard 12 commercial vessels in the Persian Gulf. Lloyd's List reports the KOTC tanker was struck in the strait; that incident was first carried by this feed on 2026-09-28, and the attacker has not been identified. Zerohedge.com, with the same claim carried by Lloyd's List, reports Iran struck a large crude tanker overnight, attributing responsibility to Iran; UKMTO has described the weapon in comparable incidents as an unknown projectile and has not identified an attacker. gCaptain reports the maritime picture is becoming harder to verify, with delayed reporting of vessel strikes raising questions about how much of the fighting is reaching the public record. On the diplomatic track, ABC10 reports U.S.-Iran talks continue after President Trump rejected Iran's strait-reopening proposal, and Caliber.Az reports Iran is awaiting a U.S. response on its proposal. Forty-two events were indexed in the past 24 hours. As of 02:50 UTC, 258 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
